of the internal names work from my machine host_1_1_1_1 -- web0.local,

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- internal names do not resolve -- is NOT reproducible:
the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) is answering, and from host_1_1_1_1
nslookup of web0.local / web1.local / web2.local / web3.local returns the correct
10.200.0.x addresses. The host's /etc/resolv.conf points at 10.200.0.2 and that
server's named daemon is listening on port 53.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: name resolution is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent queries the
DNS server (nslookup/dig web0.local against 10.200.0.2), gets correct answers, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the DNS daemon
dead or blaming dns_server to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the DNS resolver configuration on host_1_1_1_1 (/etc/resolv.conf – search domain). Mechanism: Unqualified hostnames (e.g., “web0”, “web1”) rely on a local search domain to be appended (e.g., “.local”) before querying DNS. With no search suffix, those lookups are sent exactly as typed and return NXDOMAIN, appearing as if “the address book is wiped,” while fully qualified names still work.

Localization: On host_1_1_1_1 we found /etc/resolv.conf contains only “nameserver 10.200.0.2” and no “search” or “domain” line. Evidence: getent hosts web0 returns nothing, while getent hosts web0.local returns “10.200.0.3 web0.local”. DNS infrastructure itself is healthy: the DNS server listens on 10.200.0.2:53 (netstat), and direct queries succeed (dig @10.200.0.2 web0.local → 10.200.0.3; web1.local → 10.200.0.4). End-to-end, http://web0.local resolves and loads from host_1_1_1_1 (curl succeeded).

Root cause: The search domain “local” is missing from host_1_1_1_1’s resolver configuration, so shortnames fail while FQDNs (e.g., web0.local) work.

Corrective fix: Restore a search suffix on host_1_1_1_1. Add “search local” (or “domain local”) to /etc/resolv.conf and ensure your network manager/DHCP client persists it. After this, “web0” and “web1” will resolve as “web0.local” and “web1.local”. Alternatively, update bookmarks to use fully qualified names (web0.local, web1.local), which already resolve correctly. No changes are required on the DNS server.
